newsitem.title: USA: Harkin says speculation on governor bid premature.
newsitem.headline: Harkin says speculation on governor bid premature.

text.p: Sen. Tom Harkin, under pressure from Iowa Democrats to quit the Senate and run for governor, is talking like a candidate but says speculation about his future is premature.

"Don't try reading tea leaves," he said in a weekend interview on Iowa Public Television in response to questions about a recent property purchase in the state and the fact that his wife quit her job in Washington.
But he added he intended to be "heavily involved" in setting the agenda for the state's next governor -- a post Republicans have held for the past 28 years.
"We need some new leadership in this state, bold innovative leadership that challenges the people of this state to do better. That's what I bring to the table," he said in the programme aired Sunday.

"I bring a lot of experience. I bring a lot of battles that I've been in, in the past, and I think I bring to the table a new concept, a new vision and I think some boldness in leadership that the state of Iowa needs," he added.
Republican Gov. Terry Branstad has been in office since 1983 and has served longer than any U.S. governor. He won a fourth four-year term in 1994.

During his last campaign, Branstad said he would not seek a fifth term. But Branstad has shown signs of changing his mind, though his spokesman said Monday that he has made no official decision. The filing deadline for the Iowa governor's race is March, 1998.
Harkin, who once sought his party's presidential nomination, was reelected last November to his third Senate term.
"I want to make Iowa the jewel of the Midwest," Harkin said in the television interview. "That means we have to make some bold decisions now and put out a new agenda ..."
